chunks: And it has also been narrated that he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, every people who adhere to a certain belief, the ruling of that belief applies to them.'
So if the Magians believe in the validity of that, then their marriage should be considered valid.
And also, if that were not valid, it would be necessary that it also not be valid when contracted on non-forbidden things, and the dowry was made to be wine or pork or other of the forbidden items.
Because that is not valid in the Sharia, and our companions have agreed on the validity of that.
Thus, it is known from all of this that what we mentioned is the correct view, and action should be taken upon it, while other views are discarded and not acted upon in any case.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the marriage of Magians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs the principle of *tarkib al-din* (custom of the sect) to validate Zoroastrian marriages, arguing that since they adhere to their own religious laws, their contracts are binding unless explicitly prohibited by Sharia. He reinforces this by citing the consensus (*ijma*) of the Shia scholars on the validity of dowries consisting of prohibited items like wine or pork, demonstrating that the substance of the contract remains valid despite the specific elements involved. This establishes a robust jurisprudential basis for recognizing the personal status laws of *Ahl al-Kitab* within the Shia legal framework.
